bluetooth_classic.notes: Classic Bluetooth carries audio only, and this spec does not document it beyond this block. The Classic address is public and fixed; the LE address is random and rotates, so the two never match and a client cannot find one from the other by address (the upstream author's Motif II A.N.C.; the other models were not checked). That unit's Classic address carried OUI 00:25:D1, registered to Eastern Asia Technology Limited (an ODM); one unit, so it is not offered as an identifier.

enter_pairing_mode.indicator: Headphones and earbuds: LED pulses or blinks blue. Willen: slow red pulse.
enter_pairing_mode.notes: The pairing window's length is not stated in any manual read. Motif II A.N.C. will not switch source while playing; pause first.

pairing.notes: The Classic side's story, from the manuals: the owner pairs from the host's Bluetooth settings with no PIN shown, which points at Secure Simple Pairing; the association model is not established, hence security_mode unknown. The LE control link's own pairing is device.pairing.

unpair.notes: A host can forget the product at any time; the product itself keeps its eight most recent hosts and drops the oldest (manual wording: "remembers the last 8"). A factory reset clears them all.

profiles.notes: Music. Named by the upstream write-up; not examined.
Remote control of playback. Named by the upstream write-up; not examined. The headphones and earbuds also take calls, so HFP is very likely present; not recorded.

identity.notes: The LE advertising address is random and changes between sessions, so it is a connection locator, never an identity. Once bonded, the host stack resolves the rotating address to the device's identity address with the bond's IRK and presents the device under it; that is the first key. Before a bond exists, read Serial Number String (00002a25-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb) after connecting (whether it is readable without encryption is not established). The Classic address is public and fixed but is not visible in an LE scan; the successor app reads a six-byte address out of the manufacturer data (see protocol_details.advertisement), which may be that Classic address -- hypothesis.

manufacturer_data.description: Marshall Group AB manufacturer data. From the successor app's scanner; not established on the Zound-era models. See protocol_details.advertisement for the payload layout that app parses.

host_compatibility.basis: Upstream author's BlueZ pairing notes on a Motif II A.N.C. (c0ffee-audio/marshall-protocol README).
host_compatibility.notes: Works once a pairing agent is registered: RegisterAgent with capability "NoInputNoOutput", RequestDefaultAgent, then Device1.Pair() on the LE device object (random address, " [LE]" name). Without an agent the Just Works bond is not completed. The Classic device object (public address) reports ServicesResolved but never exposes GATT; clients must use the LE object, which BlueZ lists separately.

host_compatibility.basis: The vendor app is an Android app driving the platform GATT client, and bonds with the platform's own bond call.

manufacturer_data.description: Marshall Group AB's own Bluetooth SIG company identifier (1626). The successor Marshall app looks for manufacturer data under this id when it scans (and also under the byte-swapped value 23046 = 0x5A06, a tolerance for a firmware that writes the id big-endian; 0x5A06 is not a Marshall allocation and is deliberately not listed). Whether the Zound-era models the Marshall Bluetooth app covers (Major IV 2020, Motif II A.N.C. 2023) carry it is not established. Hypothesis-level signal: rank on it, confirm by service discovery.

identification.notes: The strongest signal is only visible after connecting: primary service fa302d24-d775-4343-b9ed-8cc68ace3284 with 1337-suffixed characteristics. Whether that service UUID is also in the advertisement is not recorded, so it is deliberately not listed as an advertised UUID here. The name prefixes are the two defaults the sources show ("MOTIF II A.N.C. [LE]" from the upstream author's unit, "MONITOR III A.N.C. [LE]" from the vendor manual); the device-name characteristic lets an owner rename a unit, after which only the " [LE]" suffix matcher in discovery and the company id remain. Do NOT match on service 0000fe8f: that is the Tymphany speaker protocol (see device.notes), not this surface. MAC prefixes are useless on the LE side, whose address is random and rotates.

device.name: Marshall Bluetooth Headphones, Earbuds and Speakers (Zound BLE control)
device.notes:
Marshall-branded headphones, true-wireless earbuds and portable / home Bluetooth speakers built by Zound Industries (now Marshall Group AB). They are dual-mode: music and calls go over Classic Bluetooth (A2DP, AVRCP), and every setting the Marshall Bluetooth app changes (noise control, EQ, volume, auto-off, touch lock, rename, ...) goes over a separate BLE GATT link. The BLE side advertises under its own random address, which changes between sessions, with the product name followed by " [LE]" (for example "MOTIF II A.N.C. [LE]"). The Monitor III A.N.C. manual itself tells owners to remove both "MONITOR III A.N.C." and "MONITOR III A.N.C. [LE]" from the phone's Bluetooth list before a reset, which is the vendor's own confirmation of the naming convention.
CONTROL SURFACE. Proprietary characteristics sit under primary service fa302d24-d775-4343-b9ed-8cc68ace3284 and follow the pattern 0000{code}-1337-1dea-feed-c0ffee70c0de. Older firmware exposes the same functions as legacy 16-bit codes on the Bluetooth base (0000aaXX-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb). A client resolves every function modern UUID first, then the legacy one (both apps keep the pair as an ordered two-entry list and take the first the device has). The full code table, with each legacy alias, is in protocol_details.uuid_schemes. Standard services carry Device Information (0x2a24-0x2a29), Battery Level (0x2a19) and Battery Level Status (0x2bed). Earbud and charging-case battery levels come from a separate UUID base, 7a573e5d-9330-4d9b-8660-63c33fc5XXXX.
WHAT IS DOCUMENTED TO THE BYTE: only two things. Noise control (code 0x0013) is one byte, 0x00 off / 0x01 ANC / 0x02 transparency. EQ settings (code 0x0017) take two writes: [0x01, step, preset] assigns one of twelve presets to one of three step slots, then [0x00, step] makes that slot active. Every other characteristic is listed by UUID and role only; its payload is unknown, and nothing here guesses at it.
AUTH. The proprietary characteristics need a BLE bond. Just Works (NoInputNoOutput) is accepted. The vendor app starts that bond itself when the Classic side is already bonded and the LE side is not, except on models where the bond is derived across transports automatically; the upstream author reports that a direct LE Just Works bond with no Classic bond at all also works. On BlueZ the Classic device object never exposes GATT, even after ServicesResolved: control is only reachable on the separate LE device object.
CHIPSETS AND UPDATES. Three update families, split by chipset: Qualcomm GAIA on Major IV and Monitor III A.N.C., Airoha OTA on the Motif II A.N.C. (Airoha AB1565), and Tymphany ("Joplin") OTA on speakers such as Willen, Stanmore and Woburn. They are named in `features` and nothing more.
FAMILY CAUTION -- THE TYMPHANY-BUILT SPEAKERS. Two open-source clients for the Stanmore II and Acton II (rabbit-aaron/marshall-stanmore-2 and elrobertocarlos/marshall_bluetooth_speaker) drive those speakers through a completely different GATT set: advertised service 0000fe8f, 128-bit per-function characteristics (volume 44fa50b2-..., playback control 4446cf5f-..., EQ 31fbb033-..., and so on), not the 1337 codes. The successor Marshall app keeps that table in its Tymphany speaker path, and there it uses fa302d24-d775-4343-b9ed-8cc68ace3284 as a firmware-update CHARACTERISTIC, not as the control service. So the surface in this spec is established for the Zound-protocol headphones and earbuds (the upstream write-up's worked example is the Motif II A.N.C.); on the speakers, which of the two surfaces a given model and firmware speaks is not established. Probe the GATT table before assuming either.
Evidence base: the upstream write-up (c0ffee-audio/marshall-protocol), derived from static analysis of com.zoundindustries.marshallbt v3.7.1 and its author's BlueZ pairing session on a Motif II A.N.C.; this project's static read of the successor app com.marshallgroup.marshall v1.3.2, used only to cross-check; the vendor manuals for the button procedures. No capture exists in either source. Everything is `reported`; nothing has been run against hardware here.

openness.notes: Zound (renamed Marshall Group AB in 2023) publishes no BLE protocol documentation. Everything here was recovered from the vendor apps by third parties and by this project.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The upstream author bonded the LE side directly with Just Works; the write-up does not say whether the product was in its Classic pairing mode at the time, or whether the " [LE]" advertiser accepts a new bond whenever it is advertising. If a bond is refused, try again with the product in pairing mode (the button procedures are under bluetooth_classic.pairing.enter_pairing_mode).

exclusivity.notes: The Classic side is multipoint on some models (Monitor III A.N.C.: two hosts at once, eight remembered). Nothing says whether the LE side is.
exclusivity.recovery: If the vendor app on a phone is holding the LE link, close it (or turn off that phone's Bluetooth) before connecting from another client. Whether the product accepts a second LE central at the same time is not recorded.

pairing.notes: Proprietary characteristics require an encrypted, bonded LE link; the product accepts Just Works (NoInputNoOutput), so no PIN or passkey is involved. Two routes lead there: a direct LE bond (reported to work on a Motif II A.N.C. with no Classic bond), or the vendor app's route, which calls for an LE bond after connecting when the Classic side is bonded and the LE side is not. On models whose firmware derives the LE keys from the Classic bond automatically, the app skips that step; which models those are is in the app's per-model table, which is not reproduced here. The Motif II A.N.C. is reported as NOT one of them. Standard Device Information and Battery reads may or may not need the bond; not recorded.

unpair.notes: A factory reset deletes every pairing (see setup.factory_reset). The vendor app has a "forget device" function and a connection-control characteristic (code 0x0034), but neither's payload is documented, so no way to drop one LE bond short of a reset is established. On the client side, remove both the plain and the " [LE]" entries.

issued_to_client: The LE bond (LTK and the product's IRK), held by the host Bluetooth stack; there is no application-layer token
credentials.notes: No application-layer secret was found in either source: once the link is encrypted, the characteristics are plain reads and writes.
stored_on_device: LE bond keys (LTK, and the client's IRK if distributed) for each bonded client
Classic link keys for up to 8 remembered hosts (per the Motif II A.N.C. and Monitor III A.N.C. manuals)

factory_reset.description: Procedures below are transcribed from the vendor manuals and have not been performed here. The manuals also describe non-destructive restarts, which are worth trying first: Motif II A.N.C., put the earbuds in the case and close the lid, or hold the touch surface on both earbuds for 10 s; Monitor III A.N.C., hold the control knob for 10 s. No factory-reset procedure was found in the Major IV quick-start guide, and the Stanmore and Woburn generations this family covers are not pinned down, so neither is listed.
factory_reset.effect: Deletes all user settings and every remembered pairing; the product must be set up again. Firmware updates survive (the Willen manual says so explicitly). Afterwards, remove both the plain entry and the " [LE]" entry from each host's Bluetooth list before pairing again.

Press and hold the case button for 10 seconds, until the LED turns purple.

With the headphones on, push and hold the M-button and the ANC button together for 5 seconds; release when the LED turns purple.

methods.description: Scan for the product's " [LE]" advertisement, connect to that random address and bond with Just Works (IO capability NoInputNoOutput). The upstream author reports this works on a Motif II A.N.C. with no prior Classic bond. On BlueZ, register a NoInputNoOutput agent before calling Pair() on the LE device object, or the pairing request has nobody to answer it.
methods.name: Direct LE bond, Just Works, no Classic pairing needed

steps.action: Power the product on (earbuds: in the case with the lid open; headphones and speakers: switched on).
Scan for an LE advertisement whose local name ends in " [LE]" (or carries company id 0x065A); note its current random address.
steps.expect: A random-address advertiser named, for example, "MOTIF II A.N.C. [LE]". The Classic entry (no suffix, public address) is a different device object on most host stacks.

steps.action: Connect and bond using Just Works (NoInputNoOutput). On BlueZ: RegisterAgent(path, "NoInputNoOutput"), RequestDefaultAgent(path), then Device1.Pair() on the LE object.
steps.expect: Bond completes with no prompt on the product.

steps.action: Discover services and find fa302d24-d775-4343-b9ed-8cc68ace3284. For each function, look up the modern 1337 characteristic first and fall back to its legacy aaXX alias.
steps.expect: The proprietary characteristics read and write; before the bond they are refused.

causes: The client is looking at the Classic (public-address) device object. BlueZ does not expose GATT there; connect to the separate " [LE]" object instead.
troubleshooting.symptom: GATT services never appear although the headphones show as connected and ServicesResolved is true.

causes: No pairing agent is registered. Register a NoInputNoOutput agent and make it the default before pairing.
troubleshooting.symptom: Pair() fails or hangs on Linux.

causes: The LE address rotates between sessions. Re-scan and match by name or bond identity, not by the old address.
troubleshooting.symptom: A known LE address no longer answers.

methods.description: The vendor app's own route. The owner pairs the product for audio from the phone's Bluetooth settings (Classic pairing mode, see bluetooth_classic.pairing), then the app connects over LE. On models where keys are derived across transports automatically, the LE link is already bonded; on the others, including the Motif II A.N.C., the app starts an LE bond itself when it finds the Classic side bonded and the LE side not. Useful when a host stack derives LE keys from a Classic bond; otherwise the primary route is simpler.
methods.name: Pair audio first, then let the LE bond follow the Classic one

steps.action: Put the product in Classic pairing mode (model-specific button, see bluetooth_classic.pairing.enter_pairing_mode) and pair it from the host's Bluetooth settings.
steps.expect: The product appears as its plain name (no " [LE]") and connects for audio.

steps.action: Connect to the " [LE]" advertiser. If the LE link is not already bonded, start a bond (Just Works).
Discover services and resolve characteristics modern-first, legacy-second.

setup.notes: Nothing is provisioned: there is no Wi-Fi, no account and no cloud step between a client and the control surface. A client does need a BLE bond before the proprietary characteristics answer (see device.pairing), so the methods below are the two ways to get one. Confidence medium: the route is a third party's observation on one Motif II A.N.C. under BlueZ plus static analysis; not run here.

rejoin.notes: No network binds the product. A new client bonds the same way the first one did. The Motif II A.N.C. and Monitor III A.N.C. manuals say the product remembers up to 8 Classic hosts (Monitor III A.N.C. connects to two at once); how many LE bonds it keeps, and whether a new one evicts an old one, is not recorded.

variants.notes: True-wireless earbuds with charging case, Airoha AB1565 (per the firmware revision string upstream read, which names Airoha's AB1565 SDK). The upstream write-up's worked example: ANC, EQ, earbud and case battery. FCC ID 2AAGF-MOTIFII (granted 2023-07-23).

On-ear headphones, Qualcomm (GAIA update path). FCC ID 2AAGF-MAJORIV (granted 2020-09-21). Which characteristics it exposes is not recorded; it has no ANC hardware. Its LE advertised name is not recorded (the quick-start guide shows "Major IV" in the Classic list).
Over-ear ANC headphones, Qualcomm (GAIA update path). Its manual names the "MONITOR III A.N.C. [LE]" entry. Which characteristics it exposes is not recorded.

Small portable speaker, Tymphany/Joplin update path per upstream (which spells it "Willem"). FCC ID 2AAGF-WILLEN (granted 2022-02-23). Whether it speaks the 1337 surface or the Tymphany speaker GATT set is not established (see device.notes).

Home Bluetooth speaker, Tymphany/Joplin update path per upstream; generation not stated. The Stanmore II is driven by open-source clients through the Tymphany speaker GATT set (service 0000fe8f), not the 1337 surface, so nothing in `entities` is scoped to it.
Home Bluetooth speaker, Tymphany/Joplin update path per upstream; generation not stated. Same caution as Stanmore.

entities.name: Noise Control
entities.notes: Scoped to the ANC models. The Motif II A.N.C. is the upstream worked example; the Monitor III A.N.C. is included because it has ANC hardware and its manual sends noise-control settings through the app, not because anyone has read its GATT table. Notifications arrive when the mode changes from the product's own button.

entities.name: EQ Preset (Slot 1)
entities.notes: Half of a two-write change. Picking a preset writes [0x01, 0x00, preset] (assign it to slot 1); the sound changes only once slot 1 is active, which is the Active EQ Slot control below ([0x00, 0x00]). The schema has no way to bind a two-command sequence to one role, so the two halves are two controls. No current-value decode is declared: the read side's two shapes are not established well enough to bind (see protocol_details.eq_settings.read_forms).

entities.name: Active EQ Slot
entities.notes: Writes [0x00, slot]. Select Slot 1 after changing EQ Preset (Slot 1) to hear the new preset. No current-value decode is declared (see the preset control's note).

entities.name: Battery
entities.notes: Standard Battery Level. Scoped to the battery-powered models; which of them actually expose it is not recorded, and on the earbuds it is not established whether it reports the buds, the case or one of them (the per-bud and case levels are on the 7a573e5d-... characteristics, whose payload is undocumented and so bound to nothing).

artifacts.description: Primary source for the UUID tables, the two documented encodings, the OTA families and the pairing behaviour.

Cross-check only: confirmed the modern/legacy pairs, the ANC byte, the EQ write shapes and the company id; found fa302d24 used as a Tymphany update characteristic; did not contain the Tymphany battery UUIDs.
Negative finding for this spec: the Stanmore II speaks a different, Tymphany GATT set.
Same negative finding for the Acton II and Stanmore II; discovers them by service 0000fe8f.

artifacts.artifact: Marshall user manuals: Motif II A.N.C. R0.13, Major IV quick start, Monitor III A.N.C., Willen
artifacts.description: Button procedures for pairing and factory reset; the [LE] entry named in the Monitor III A.N.C. manual.
Grantee Zound Industries International AB; 2.4 GHz grants. Not otherwise used.

evidence.documentation_review: Vendor manuals for the Motif II A.N.C., Major IV (quick start), Monitor III A.N.C. and Willen: pairing and factory-reset button procedures, the eight-host memory, and the Monitor III A.N.C. manual's mention of the " [LE]" Bluetooth-list entry. FCC grant pages for 2AAGF-MOTIFII, 2AAGF-MAJORIV and 2AAGF-WILLEN (Zound Industries International AB).
evidence.open_questions: Every payload beyond noise control and the EQ writes. The exact LE name per model. Which characteristics each model exposes. Which firmware versions moved from the legacy to the modern scheme. Whether the Tymphany speakers speak this surface at all. Whether fa302d24 is advertised. The EQ read forms. See remaining_unknowns.
evidence.successor_app_cross_check: This project's static read of the successor app com.marshallgroup.marshall v1.3.2 (Google Play, 2026-08), used only to check the upstream facts. It repeats every modern/legacy pair from 0x0001 to 0x0025 except 0x000c, reads and writes noise control as the same single byte 0/1/2, builds the EQ writes exactly as [0x01, step, preset] and [0x00, step], and scans for manufacturer data under company id 1626. It also uses fa302d24-... as a firmware-update characteristic in its Tymphany speaker path, and carries the Tymphany speaker GATT table. The Tymphany battery UUIDs are not in it.
evidence.upstream_hardware_notes: The same README's connection and pairing section reports a session on its author's own Motif II A.N.C. under BlueZ: separate public (Classic) and random (LE) addresses, the " [LE]" name, a Just Works bond after registering a NoInputNoOutput agent, and no GATT on the Classic device object. Third-party observation, not a capture; the author's addresses are not reproduced.
evidence.upstream_static_analysis: c0ffee-audio/marshall-protocol (README): characteristic codes and legacy aliases, properties, the service UUID, the ANC byte, the EQ two-write sequence and preset ids, the Tymphany battery UUIDs, the OTA families, and the auth rules, all from static analysis of the Android app com.zoundindustries.marshallbt v3.7.1. Its per-model feature map comes from an app enum and is not reproduced. The repository carries no licence, so this spec restates its facts in its own words and tables.

dfu.notes: Qualcomm GAIA, on the headphones with a Qualcomm chip. Its GATT attributes use the Qualcomm base 0000xxxx-d102-11e1-9b23-00025b00a5a5. `custom` because the mechanism vocabulary has no GAIA member (`csr_ota` names the older CSR OTA service 00001016 on that base, a different protocol). Named only: no transfer or entry bytes are documented, because a wrong or interrupted image can leave headphones unusable. Whether the app also runs GAIA over Classic RFCOMM is not recorded.
Airoha OTA, on the Airoha AB1565 earbuds. Named only: no transport details, transfer or entry bytes are documented here. An interrupted earbud update may leave a bud unbootable.

Tymphany ("Joplin") OTA, on the Tymphany-built speakers. Named only. One finding from the successor app is recorded because it collides with the control service: in that app's Tymphany path, fa302d24-d775-4343-b9ed-8cc68ace3284 is the update CHARACTERISTIC (under a 16-bit service), so on these speakers the UUID may mark the update path rather than the control surface. No bytes are documented.

initialization.description: Make sure the link is bonded and encrypted before touching any proprietary characteristic; unbonded reads and writes are refused. A client that connected to an already-bonded product gets encryption from the stored keys; otherwise bond first (Just Works, see device.pairing).

Resolve each function's characteristic by UUID across all discovered services: the modern 0000{code}-1337-1dea-feed-c0ffee70c0de UUID first, and only if it is absent the legacy 0000aaXX alias on the Bluetooth base (table in protocol_details.uuid_schemes). A function with neither is not supported by that model or firmware; hide its control rather than showing it broken.

advertisement.local_name: Product name plus the suffix " [LE]"; the successor app strips "[LE]" and a leading "LE-" to get the display name. "LE-" is not used as a matcher here because other audio brands use that prefix.

fields.name: product_id
fields.notes: Looked up in the app's per-model table.

fields.name: colour_code
fields.notes: Finish / colourway, 0-5 in the app's table.

fields.name: address
fields.notes: Formatted by the app as a colon-separated MAC. Probably the Classic address; not established.

manufacturer_data.notes: Offsets are into the payload after the two company-id bytes.

advertisement.source: The successor Marshall app's scanner (1.3.2); not established on the Marshall Bluetooth app-era models.

long_form.notes: The successor app also carries a six-entry tone-style preset table (0 flat, 1 custom, 2 bass boost, 3 mid boost, 4 treble boost, 5 mid reduction) that is probably what preset_type 1 selects. Hypothesis.

The successor app's per-characteristic encoders are the obvious next place to read them.

change_active_step.description: Make one EQ step slot the active one (second of the two writes).

characteristics.name: EQ step settings
characteristics.notes: The product holds three EQ "step" slots (0, 1, 2) that its own button cycles through, each carrying one preset. Changing the sound is two writes: assign_step_preset puts a preset in a slot, then change_active_step makes that slot current. For a simple preset change the upstream write-up uses slot 0 both times, e.g. rock = [0x01, 0x00, 0x02] then [0x00, 0x00]. The read side has two shapes (a three-byte short form and a 0xFF-prefixed long form) whose field meanings come from the successor app only; they are in protocol_details.eq_settings.read_forms and are not declared as a `format` here. Legacy alias 0000aa25-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, same payloads.

services.name: Zound control service
services.notes: Primary service of the proprietary control surface (upstream write-up). Characteristic UUIDs are 0000{code}-1337-1dea-feed-c0ffee70c0de; each of the codes up to 0x0025 also has a legacy alias on the Bluetooth base (listed in the next entry and in protocol_details.uuid_schemes). Both vendor apps look a characteristic up by UUID across every discovered service rather than inside this one, so a client should do the same. Properties are upstream's; write type (with or without response) is not recorded, so every writable one says `write`. Only 0x0013 and 0x0017 have documented payloads. For every other characteristic here the payload layout is UNKNOWN: nothing below guesses at it, and nothing binds an entity to it. Caution: in the successor app's Tymphany-speaker path this same UUID is a firmware-update characteristic under a 16-bit service, not a service (see device.notes).

services.name: Characteristics with no recorded parent service (legacy aliases, earbud battery)
services.notes: Grouping placeholder, not a second service on the device. Holds (1) the legacy 0000aaXX aliases older firmware exposes in place of the 1337 characteristics, and (2) the earbud / case battery characteristics on the 7a573e5d-9330-4d9b-8660-63c33fc5XXXX base. Neither source records which service contains them. Look each up by UUID across all services. A legacy alias carries the same payload as its modern twin; only the two with documented payloads (noise control, EQ) and the ones a client is most likely to probe are named in full here, and the whole mapping is in protocol_details.uuid_schemes.characteristic_codes.

characteristics.name: Battery Level Status
characteristics.notes: SIG-defined structure (Battery Service 1.1): a flags byte, a 16-bit power-state bitfield, then optional identifier, level and additional-status fields as the flags say. Only the fixed head is declared; decode the rest per the SIG specification.
